title: Technical English — Course 5, Semester 2 — Pilot Variant 2

tasks.prompt: Listening 1. When will the risk-communication session take place?
tasks.audioText: The engineering safety lecturer will discuss risk communication on Monday at ten fifteen. Students should bring the risk-register example and meet in the seminar room. The session will focus on describing hazards, existing controls and remaining concerns. The lecturer will explain why risk information should be specific, current and understandable to the people who need it.
options: At ten fifteen on Monday
At nine on Tuesday
At eleven on Monday
At ten fifteen on Thursday

tasks.prompt: Listening 2. Which example should students bring?
tasks.audioText: The engineering safety lecturer will discuss risk communication on Monday at ten fifteen. Students should bring the risk-register example and meet in the seminar room. The session will focus on describing hazards, existing controls and remaining concerns. The lecturer will explain why risk information should be specific, current and understandable to the people who need it.
options: The inspection checklist
The risk-register example
The maintenance schedule
The component glossary

tasks.prompt: A risk record should describe a hazard, the possible consequence and the controls that are already in place. It should also identify any remaining concern and the person or team responsible for review. A risk rating is only meaningful when the method and assumptions are clear. If conditions change, the record should be reviewed rather than treated as permanently valid. Reading 1. What should a risk record describe?
options: Only the name of the hazard
The personal opinions of the maintenance team
The hazard, possible consequence, existing controls and remaining concern
The cost of every component in the system

tasks.prompt: When should a risk record be reviewed?
options: At the end of every calendar month only
When a new student joins the course
When the report is printed
When conditions change

tasks.prompt: The risk record ___ when working conditions change.
options: should be reviewed
should review
reviewing
are reviewed yesterday

tasks.prompt: Choose TWO features of clear risk communication.
options: A vague statement with no context
An assumption that conditions never change
A specific description of the hazard
A clear explanation of existing controls

tasks.prompt: A source of potential harm or adverse effect is a ___.
A risk record does not explain who will review an outstanding concern. What should you ask?
options: The responsible person is not important.
Could we identify who is responsible for reviewing the remaining concern?
The concern should be removed from the record.
I will assign a person without checking.

tasks.prompt: Put the stages of risk communication in a logical order.
options: Identify remaining concerns and responsibility
Describe the hazard and possible consequence
Review the record when conditions change
Record existing controls
correctOrder: Describe the hazard and possible consequence
Review the record when conditions change

tasks.prompt: Write 100–120 words explaining how to communicate a technical risk clearly. Include a hazard, consequence, control and review responsibility.
tasks.rubric: 8 points total: task completion and relevant content (0–2); clear organisation and logical linking (0–2); grammar and sentence structure (0–2); precise technical vocabulary, spelling and punctuation (0–2). Minor errors are acceptable if meaning remains clear.
